newsitem.title: USA: LIST OF GRAMMY AWARD WINNERS.
newsitem.headline: LIST OF GRAMMY AWARD WINNERS.

text.p: The following is a list of
winners of the 39th annual Grammy music industry awards:
Producer of the Year: Babyface.
Album of the Year: Celine Dion, "Falling Into You."
Record of the Year: Eric Clapton, "Change the World."
Song of the Year: Gordon Kennedy, Wayne Kirkpatrick and
Tommy Sims for "Change the World."
Best New Artist: LeAnn Rimes.
Best Spoken Word or Non-Musical Album: Hillary Rodham
Clinton, "It Takes A Village."
Best Rock Album: Sheryl Crow, "Sheryl Crow."
Best Male Rock Vocal Performance: Beck, "Where It's At"
(Track from "Odelay").
Best Female Rock Vocal Performance: Sheryl Crow, "If It
Makes You Happy" (Track from "Sheryl Crow").
Best Alternative Music Performance: Beck, "Odelay."
Best Rock Song: Tracy Chapman, "Give Me One Reason" (Track
from "New Beginning").
Best Rock Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocal: Dave
Matthews Band, "So Much to Say" (Track from "Crash").
Best Hard Rock Performance: The Smashing Pumpkins, "Bullet
with Butterfly Wings."
Best Metal Performance: Rage Against the Machine, "Tire Me"
(Track from "Evil Empire")
Best Rock Instrumental Performance: SRV Shuffle (Jimmie
Vaughan, Eric Clapton, Bonnie Raitt, Robert Cray, B.B. King,
Buddy Guy, Dr. John and Art).
Best Pop Album: Celine Dion, "Falling Into You."
Best Female Pop Vocal Performance: Toni Braxton, "Un-Break
My Heart" (Track from "Secrets").
Best Male Pop Vocal Performance: Eric Clapton, "Change the
World" (Track from "Phenomenon").
Best Pop Collaboration with Vocals: Natalie Cole (and Nat
King Cole), (Track from "Stardust").
Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocal: "Free as
a Bird", the Beatles (Track from "Anthology 1").
Best Pop Instrumental Performance: Bela Fleck & The
Flecktones, "The Sinister Minister" (Track from "Live Art").
Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance: Tony Bennett,
"Here's to the Ladies."
Best R&B Album: The Tony Rich Project, "Words."
Best R&B Song (songwriter's award): Babyface for "Exhale
(Shoop Shoop)" performed by Whitney Houston (Track from
"Waiting to Exhale-Soundtrack").
Best R&B Solo Performance: LL Cool J, "Hey Lover" (Track
from "Mr.Smith")
Best R&B Duo or Group Performance with Vocal: Fugees,
"Killing Me Softly With His Song," (Track From "The Score").
Best Female R&B Vocal Performance: Toni Braxton, "You're
Makin' Me High" (Track from "Secrets").
Best Male R&B Performance: Luther Vandross, "Your Secret
Love" (Track from "Your Secret Love")
Best Rap Album: Fugees, "The Score."
Best Rap Solo Performance: LL Cool J, "Hey Lover" (Track
from "Mr. Smith").
Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group: Bone
Thugs-N-Harmony, "Tha Crossroads" (Track from E. 1999 Eternal).
Best Jazz Vocal Performance: Cassandra Wilson, "New Moon
Daughter."
Best Jazz Instrumental Solo: Michael Brecker, "Cabin Fever"
(Track from "Tales from the Hudson").
Best Jazz Instrumental Performance: Michael Brecker, "Tales
from the Hudson."
Best Contemporary Jazz Performance: Wayne Shorter, "High
Life."
Best Latin Jazz Performance: Paquito D'Rivera, "Portraits
of Cuba."
Best Large Jazz Ensemble Performance: "Live At Manchester
Craftsmen's Guild," Count Basie Orchestra.
Best Rock Gospel Album: dc Talk, "Jesus Freak."
Best Pop/Contemporary Gospel Album: Various Artists,
"Tribute: The Songs of Andrae Crouch."
Best Southern Gospel, Country Gospel or Bluegrass Gospel
Album: Andy Griffith, "I Love to Tell the Story -- 25 Timeless
Hymns."
Best Traditional Soul Gospel Album: Cissy Houston, "Face to
Face."
Best Contemporary Soul Gospel Album: Kirk Franklin & The
Family, "Whatcha Lookin' 4."
Best Latin Pop Performance: Enrique Iglesias, "Enrique
Iglesias."
Best Tropical Latin Performance: Ruben Blades, "La Rosa de
los Vientos."
Best Mexican-American/Tejano Music Performance: La Mafia,
"Un Million de Rosas."
Best Contemporary Folk Album: Bruce Springsteen, "The Ghost
of Tom Joad."
Best Traditional Folk Album: Pete Seeger, "Pete."
Best Musical Show Album: "Riverdance."
Best Traditional Blues Album: James Cotton, "Deep in the
Blues."
Best Contemporary Blues Album: Keb' Mo', "Just Like You."
Best Classical Vocal Performance: Bryn Terfel, "Opera Arias
(Works of Mozart, Wagner, Borodin, etc.)."
Best Classical Album: "Corigliano: Of Rage and
Rememberance."
Classical Producer of the Year: Joanna Nickrenz.
Best Orchestral Performance: "Prokofiev: Romeo & Juliet
(Scenes from the Ballet)".
Best Opera Recordings: "Britten: Peter Grimes."
Best Choral Performance: "Walton: Belshazzar's Feast."
Best Instrumental Soloist Performance (without Orchestra):
"The Romantic Master (Works of Saint-Saens, Handel, Etc.)."
Best Instrumental Soloist (with Orchestra): Yefim Bronfman,
"Bartok: The Three Piano Concertos."
Best Chamber Music Performance: "Corigliano: String
Quartet," Cleveland Quartet.
Best Classical Contemporary Composition: "Corigliano:
String Quartet."
Best Small Ensemble Performance: "Boulez:
...Explosante-Fixe..."
Best Instrumental Composition: Herbie Hancock and Jean
Hancock, "Manhattan (Island of Lights and Love)" (Track from
"The New Standard").
Best Instrumental Composition Written for a Motion Picture
or Television: "Independence Day."
Best Song Written for a Motion Picture or Television: Diane
Warren for Celine Dion, "Because You Loved Me" (From "Up Close
and Personal"), performed by Celine Dion.
Best Instrumental Arrangement: Michael Kamen and the London
Metropolitan Orchestra, "Mr. Holland's Opus."
Best Instrumental Arrangement with Accompanying Vocals:
"When I Fall in Love" by Alan Broadbent and David Foster.
Best Recording Package: "Ultra-Lounge (Leopard Skin
Sampler)", Various Artists.
Best Recording Package-Boxed: "The Complete Columbia Studio
Recordings", Miles Davis and Gil Evans.
Best Album Notes: "The Complete Columbia Studio
Recordings", Miles Davis and Gil Evans.
Best Historical Album: "The Complete Studio Recordings",
Miles Davis and Gil Evans.
Best Reggae Album: Bunny Wailer, "Hall of Fame -- A Tribute
to Bob Marley's 50th Anniversary."
Best World Music: The Chieftains, "Santiago."
Best Country Album: Lyle Lovett, "The Road to Ensenada."
Best Country Song (songwriter's award): Bill Mack for
"Blue", performed by LeAnn Rimes (Track from "Blue").
Best Female Country Vocal Performance: LeAnn Rimes, "Blue"
(Track from "Blue").
Best Male Country Vocal Performance: Vince Gill, "Worlds
Apart" (Track from "High Lonesome Sound").
Best Country Performance by a Duo or Group: Brooks & Dunn,
"My Maria" (Track from "Borderline").
Best Country Collaboration with Vocals: Vince Gill, "High
Lonesome Sound" (Track from "High Lonesome Sound").
Best Country Instrumental Performance: Chet Atkins C.G.P.,
"Jam Man" (Track from "Almost Alone").
Best Bluegrass Album: Various Artists, "True Life Blues:
The Songs of Bill Monroe."
Best New Age Album: Enya, "The Memory of Trees."
Best Polka Album: Jimmy Sturr, "Polka! All Night Long."
Best Musical Album for Children: Linda Ronstadt, "Dedicated
to the One I Love."
Best Spoken Word Album for Children: David Holt,
"Stellaluna."
Best Spoken Comedy Album: Al Franken, "Rush Limbaugh is a
Big Fat Idiot."
Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical: Various Artists, "Q's
Jook Joint."
Best Classical Engineered Recording: "Copland: Dance
Symphony; Short Symphony; Organ Symphony, Etc.," conducted by
Leonard Slotkin.
Best Music Video, Short Form: the Beatles, "Free As a
Bird."
Best Music Video, Long Form: the Beatles, "The Beatles
Anthology."
